Evidence

Research and Reference Libraries

This site is built from primary sources rather than opinion. Here is every library it draws on, what each one contains, and how to read it responsibly.

Home/Research

A claim is only as good as the source behind it. Rather than asking you to trust this website, the libraries below let you go straight to the original material — regulator guidance, public-health information, systematic reviews and the peer-reviewed record.

How to read research responsibly

An archive is not a recommendation service. A published paper can be small, observational, outdated or contradicted by later work. Systematic reviews and randomised trials sit at the top of the evidence ladder; single-centre case series and manufacturer surveys sit near the bottom. Before changing a treatment decision, read the full article, check its date and design, and discuss it with a qualified clinician.
